definitions.explanation: A person or group chasing after someone who is fleeing. Often used in historical, literary, or dramatic contexts involving fugitives or escapes.

examples.japanese: {追|お}っ{手|て}が{迫|せま}ってきた。
{追|お}っ{手|て}をまいて{山|やま}に{逃|に}げ{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: He shook off the pursuers and fled into the mountains.

examples.japanese: {藩|はん}は{脱走|だっそう}した{侍|さむらい}を{捕|と}らえるために、すぐに{追|お}っ{手|て}を{差|さ}し{向|む}けた。
examples.english: The domain immediately dispatched pursuers to capture the escaped samurai.

notes:
Refers to those who chase a fugitive or escapee. Common in historical fiction, period dramas, and action narratives.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {追|お}っ{手|て}をかける (to send pursuers after)
- {追|お}っ{手|て}を{差|さ}し{向|む}ける (to dispatch pursuers)
- {追|お}っ{手|て}をまく (to shake off pursuers)
- {追|お}っ{手|て}から{逃|に}げる (to flee from pursuers)

The word has a dramatic, literary quality and appears frequently in {時代劇|じだいげき} (period dramas) and historical novels.
